newsitem.title: USA: Ill. Gov pushes school finance reform, GO bonds.
newsitem.headline: Ill. Gov pushes school finance reform, GO bonds.

text.p: Illinois Gov. Jim Edgar on Wednesday renewed his push for a school funding reform plan, as well as passage of a general obligation bond bill.

In his state of the state address to the General Assembly in Springfield, Edgar called on lawmakers to pass a plan that would bring state funding of primary and secondary public schools to the 50 percent level, while providing at least $1.5 billion in property tax relief.

In addition, he called for a minimum annual level of per pupil funding of $4,225. Edgar said that while he considered the state income tax as the fairest way to raise more money for schools, he was willing to consider a combination of other revenue sources.

The school funding plan was similar to one proposed last spring by Edgar and rejected by lawmakers. In October, judicial pressure on the state was eased when the Illinois Supreme Court dismissed a constitutional challenge to the state's school funding system.

The governor also called on lawmakers to approve a GO bonding bill, whose lack of passage over the past two years he blamed on partisan politics. Previous bills have called for $610 million in GO bonding authorization for prison, university and other capital projects.
